notes: Transport is the id Tech 3 connectionless rcon (an out-of-band UDP packet "rcon <password> <command>" to the game port, handled by SVC_RemoteCommand in sv_main.c), NOT Source RCON; it is turned on simply by setting the rconPassword cvar (Cvar_Get("rconPassword", "", CVAR_TEMP)), and the port is the game port (net_port, PORT_SERVER 27960). listPlayers uses the engine's status, whose first column is the client slot number that clientkick takes; SV_Status_f prints num/score/ping-or-CNCT-or-ZMBI/name/lastmsg/address:port/qport/rate, which is what the regex reads. kick: vanilla and ET: Legacy both accept "kick <player name> [timeout]" and "clientkick <client number> [timeout]" (in id's engine both are commented out of SV_AddOperatorCommands and moved to the qagame module's ConsoleCommand; ET: Legacy maps both names to the same Svcmd_Kick_f "to keep compatibility"). The slot-number form is recorded because status yields the slot directly and names carry ^x colour codes. Careful: with no timeout argument the timeout defaults to 300, and the game module then drops the client AND temp-bans their address for that many seconds (USE_ENGINE_BANLIST is qtrue), so "clientkick <num> 0" is a pure kick with no ban. ban is recorded as "clientkick {playerId} {duration}" (duration in seconds) because it targets the slot number reliably on both vanilla 2.60b and ET: Legacy; it is an engine temp ban held in memory and lost when the server restarts. The permanent alternative is the game module's own "ban" command (G_PlayerBan), which adds the player's IP to the g_banIPs filter: on vanilla 2.60b it resolves the target with G_refClientnumForName (colour-stripped name only, usage string "ban <clientname>"), while ET: Legacy's version uses G_ClientNumberFromString and so also accepts a client number - "ban {playerId}" is therefore correct on ET: Legacy but silently misses on vanilla, hence it is not the recorded form. IP bans are managed with "addip <ip-mask>", "removeip <ip-mask>" and "listip" (the list is persisted in the g_banIPs cvar, not in a ban file), so no unban is recorded: removeip needs an IP mask rather than a player id, and ET: Legacy's engine adds "cleartempbans" which clears the entire temp list. No MOTD command exists; vanilla shows the server_motd0..server_motd5 cvars on the connect screen, set with e.g. "set server_motd0 <text>". Console say is registered only on dedicated servers and broadcasts as a centre-print prefixed "server: ". Disagreement: Legion Hosting's knowledge base lists "banClient <id>", "unban <id>" and "banlist"; banClient (and banUser) exist in id's engine only inside the dead #ifdef AUTHORIZE_SUPPORT block (they needed id's auth server), and unban/banlist exist in neither id's source nor ET: Legacy's - treat those three as wrong. Server mods (ETPub, NoQuarter, ETPro, silEnT) add their own shrubbot !kick/!ban commands on top of this; the values here are the stock console/rcon set.
